newsitem.title: POLAND: SCHRODER PICKS 3 CO-LEADERS FOR POLAND'S HANDLOWY.
newsitem.headline: SCHRODER PICKS 3 CO-LEADERS FOR POLAND'S HANDLOWY.

text.p: J. Henry Schroder, advising Poland and Bank Handlowy SA on Handlowy's privatisation, picked three investment banks as co-leaders of its institutional offering, Handlowy said on Wednesday in a statement.

It said Schroder, which will also act as global coordinator of Handlowy's public offering due late in June, chose Goldman Sachs International, Merrill Lynch International Ltd and UBS Ltd as co-lead managers and Daiwa Europe Ltd and Dresdner Kleinwort Benson as the issue's co-managers.
Handlowy said its own securities house would be responsible for managing the bank's retail offer in Poland.
"Leading investment banks were picked as members of the (offering) syndicate and its composition guarantees that the bank will be offered in several regions of the world," Handlowy said.
The treasury plans to sell in the public offering 42.9 percent of Bank Handlowy, Poland's top bank in terms of capital strength, with equally sized institutional and domestic retail tranches.
Another 42.9 percent of Handlowy is to be offered to a group of selected international financial institutions and the talks with prospective buyers are expected to be finalised around mid-year.
The government also plans to raise Handlowy's share capital through an issue of convertible bonds, proceeds from which would help finance a sweeping pension reform.

After the issue the non-public tranche, the public offering and shares resulting from bond conversion, would represent 30 percent of Handlowy's capital each. The state treasury and employees would hold five percent stakes each.
